892.supersedes: The block of 29 Oct 2026 kept the verdict partly_read without seeing any cipher and said 'no decipherment'. New evidence: the five archive records were read and all their images viewed; 8-3-12 and 9-1-2 each have a 19th-century decipherment filed with them; three of the five items are Latin, not Italian; HathiTrust full-text search finds the deciphered Latin of 8-3-12 and of 9-1-2 in Austro-Turcica. The verdict stays partly_read with these corrections.

seen.extent: 8-2-22 (Malvezzi to Ferdinand, Constantinople, 24 Mar 1550, Italian, original and copy, 8 images, partly ciphered); 8-2-24 (Ferdinand to Malvezzi, Vienna, 25 Mar 1550, Latin, about 25 cipher lines, 2 images); 8-3-10 (Malvezzi to Ferdinand, Constantinople, 22 Apr 1550, Italian, partly ciphered, 2 images); 8-3-12 (Ferdinand to Malvezzi, Brno, 28 Apr 1550, Latin, original 42 cipher lines and duplicate 29 lines, plus a 19th-century decipherment, 6 images); 9-1-2 (Ferdinand to Malvezzi, Augsburg, 3 Oct 1550, Latin, about 6 cipher lines, plus a 19th-century decipherment, 3 images).
seen.cipher: Graphic-sign homophonic cipher of Malvezzi's alphabet (signs such as circle on a stem, hash, two bars, Greek letters, numerals for doubled letters, null words Cum, Porro, Spo, Dar; code word Ras). 8-3-12 images 5-6 and 9-1-2 image 3 are 19th-century decipherments headed 'Entzifferung', giving the whole ciphered text of 8-3-12 and the ciphered passage of 9-1-2 in Latin. The original of 8-3-12 was transcribed sign by sign twice blind and decoded with the upstream malvezzi1548 key (lead892_test/).

prior_art.edition: Austro-Turcica 1541-1552, ed. Karl Nehring (Munich 1995), HathiTrust mdp.39015038445451, search only. The archive cites it for 8-2-22 pp. 415-418, 8-2-24 pp. 418-419, 8-3-10 pp. 433-434, 8-3-12 p. 437, 9-1-2 p. 513. HathiTrust full-text phrase searches on 23 Nov 2026 each returned this volume as the only hit: 'quemadmodum a Rege suo sibi iussum' and 'Transmittimus ad te cum hisce' (8-3-12) and 'de successibus omnibus certiores facere pergas' (9-1-2). So the edition prints the deciphered Latin of those two letters, not only a summary. Page numbers of the hits could not be displayed (the in-volume search page did not render); the other three items were not searched.

892.key_check: Tested on 8-3-12 (original): the upstream targets/malvezzi1548/KEY_BRIEF.md key, unchanged, decoded mechanically from the second blind transcription matches 0.924 of the 952 letters of the 19th-century decipherment (pass mark 0.85 set in a hashed plan; 200 shuffled keys mean 0.358, best 0.430); 124 of 170 words read with no supplied letter. The cipher did not change between 1548 and 1550.

892.closed: Read in the 19th century and printed: 8-3-12 (Ferdinand to Malvezzi, Brno, 28 Apr 1550) and the ciphered passage of 9-1-2 (3 Oct 1550) have 19th-century decipherments filed with them in the archive, and HathiTrust search finds their Latin in Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 (pp. 437 and 513 as cited by the archive). The upstream malvezzi1548 key reads 8-3-12 unchanged (lead892_test/). Unread: 8-2-24 (Latin, about 25 lines; clear draft at 8-2-10 fol. 74), Malvezzi's Italian letters 8-2-22 and 8-3-10, the duplicate of 8-3-12; whether Austro-Turcica prints their ciphered passages was not checked.
